issues.legal_issue: A building permission for land subject to government-estate management is invalid when the required estate officer was not consulted beforehand.
material_facts: The proposed construction was on land within a cantonment area and was subject to the statutory requirement for consultation with the relevant estate officer.
The board granted permission without first referring the application to the Defence Estates Officer.
After the superior military authority suspended the board’s resolution and directed reconsideration, the board cancelled the permission.
issues.conclusion: The permission was per se illegal because the required prior consultation had not occurred.
issues.legal_principle: Section 181(3) of the Cantonments Act requires the board, before sanctioning construction on land under military-estate management, to refer the application to the relevant estate officer to ascertain whether the Government objects. The 1983 amendment, effective from 1 October 1983, substituted “Defence Estates Officer” for “Military Estates Officer.” Compliance with this prerequisite is necessary for a valid sanction. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.cantonment_building_permission_case: A dispute concerns permission to erect or re-erect a building in a cantonment area.
predicates.land_managed_by_government_estates: The land on which construction is proposed is managed as government estate land.
predicates.prior_estate_officer_consultation_missin: The board grants permission without first referring the application to the relevant estate officer for consideration of any government objection.

issues.definition: When a cantonment building-permission dispute concerns government-estate land and the required prior consultation is missing, the permission is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Equity does not justify allowing construction to continue when the construction contravenes mandatory legal requirements.
material_facts: The respondents had started construction after receiving the board’s permission.
The permission had been granted without the required prior consultation with the Defence Estates Officer.
The High Court relied in part on the respondents’ progress with construction to find cancellation inequitable.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in extending equitable relief to facilitate completion of construction that contravened mandatory legal requirements.
issues.legal_principle: Construction carried out in contravention of law does not create an equitable entitlement to complete it or excuse non-compliance with mandatory legal requirements. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.building_permission_dispute: A dispute concerns whether construction may proceed under a building permission.
predicates.construction_has_started: The person seeking relief has begun construction.
predicates.construction_contravenes_mandatory_requi: The construction proceeds under permission granted without compliance with a mandatory legal requirement.

issues.definition: When construction has begun under a permission that fails a mandatory requirement, equity cannot authorize its completion.

issues.legal_issue: When a building permission is invalid for failure to meet a mandatory prerequisite, the appropriate course is a fresh application rather than a remand merely to provide an opportunity before cancellation.
material_facts: The board cancelled the permission without giving the respondents prior notice or an opportunity to be heard.
The permission was invalid because the required prior consultation with the Defence Estates Officer had not occurred.
The appeal challenged a High Court decision that had set aside the cancellation, and the Supreme Court directed the respondents to apply afresh for permission.
issues.conclusion: Although no prior notice had been given before cancellation, the Court did not direct a fresh cancellation proceeding with an opportunity to be heard; it directed the respondents to make a fresh application for consideration according to law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court acknowledged the absence of prior notice but treated the failure to meet the statutory prerequisite as decisive and selected a fresh application as the proper course, rather than prolonging the proceedings to require a fresh cancellation order after a hearing. Section 181(3) of the Cantonments Act supplied the unmet prerequisite. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_challenges_cancellation_of_buildi: An appeal challenges a decision concerning cancellation of permission to construct a building.
predicates.cancellation_was_without_prior_notice: The authority cancels the permission without first giving the affected applicant notice and an opportunity to be heard.
predicates.permission_lacked_mandatory_prerequisite: The permission was granted without compliance with a mandatory prerequisite for its grant.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges cancellation made without prior notice and the permission lacked a mandatory prerequisite, the applicant must make a fresh application.
